audits.resolution_reason: Easy default seed131 overwrites source cell with anchor and fails own validator; canonical multicontrol input rejected; exact controls ignored. Actual Racket labels retained; source unchanged and production materializer acceptance not established.
audits.text:
## 55ff88a3cf8f

**Findings: a default placement can overwrite the source template; three advertised overrides are ignored; the one-control validator rejects a canonical example and excludes a canonical-fitting rival's distinguishing case.** This was a findings-only audit of the immutable draw. No generator, rule, tests, assignment, or protected index was edited.

The audited generator is `repo/generators/55ff88a3cf8f/generator.py`, version `2.1.0`, SHA-256 `909cba5b96250d3c23c2cf5c3613a6213a24340a193d1a152bd4eb86067598bc`. The public Racket receipt reports canonical rule hash `964cc46a301b`, matching the catalog, and executed rule-text SHA-256 `fe4e10b3c2a71294814a3165e7cc34d4969758e9f0522e94309436d31412f074`. All coordinates below are zero-based.

### A1. An ordinary default draw overwrites one source cell and fails its own validator

The exact call `generate(seed=131, sample_index=0, difficulty="easy")`, with no overrides, returns a 14×15 grid containing only two color-6 cells. Its own `self_check` returns `color-6 source shape must have at least three cells`. This is within the ordinary default path, not an explicitly requested degenerate texture.

A temporary in-memory wrapper around `paint_at`, restored immediately after the call, retained the actual placement trace. The generator initially paints the three-cell source at `(2,11)`, `(3,11)`, `(3,12)`. It chooses control 4 at `(1,13)` and anchor `(3,12)`. The planned rotated footprint is `(3,13)`, `(4,12)`, `(4,13)`, which does not contain the anchor origin. The anchor acceptance test checks only that footprint against the occupied prototype box. It therefore accepts this placement, then writes 8 onto the original source cell `(3,12)`. The returned source is the damaged two-cell vertical segment at `(2,11)`, `(3,11)`.

Public Racket successfully labels the returned input and stamps its actual two-cell source at `(3,12)`, `(3,13)`. The input SHA-256 is `06bc180977417cc8876aa7266c1a7c78fd42e27f20876666ca1cb39489c5e70c`; output SHA-256 is `1e52bf8a0b7aad54803fb01b6fe25df283bbcbe202124874e9bd506e0d76067f`. This establishes a generator/domain failure. It does not establish incorrect Racket labeling or that a validator-enforcing materializer accepts the sample. The direct repair is to check the anchor origin for occupancy before accepting it, in addition to checking the rotated footprint.

### A2. The canonical control distractor is rejected, and control selection remains ambiguous

The authority selects the first color-1..4 cell in row-major order. Canonical variant 0, train pair 2 contains control 3 at `(0,0)` and control 4 at `(9,12)`. The current validator instead requires exactly one such cell and rejects this canonical input with `expected exactly one control cell in colors 1..4; got 2`. The other four canonical inputs pass this validator.

An independently implemented rival selects the numerically smallest control value, then performs the same source selection, rotation, anchor placement, and preservation as the authority. It matches **5/5 canonical outputs**, including train pair 2, where the first control is also the smallest. The reference-aligned Python mirror independently matches 5/5 as well. Every ordinary generated input has one control, so the reference and this rival are answer-equivalent throughout that current generated family. Adding more samples from the same grammar cannot identify the intended control-selection policy.

The retained distinguishing input changes exactly two values in canonical train pair 2: `(0,0)` becomes 4 and `(9,12)` becomes 3. Its 10×13 canvas, four-cell color-6 source, and anchor `(5,2)` otherwise remain identical. Public Racket selects the first control, 4, and rotates the T shape 270° clockwise. The rival selects 3 and rotates it 180°. Both stamps fit without overlapping the prototype. The exact output disagreements are:

| Cell | Actual Racket value | Minimum-control rival value |
|---|---:|---:|
| `(5,2)` | 8 | 3 |
| `(5,4)` | 0 | 3 |
| `(6,2)` | 3 | 0 |
| `(7,3)` | 3 | 0 |

Racket preserves the anchor at `(5,2)` because the actual rotated footprint omits that origin. The swapped input SHA-256 is `ee5489f6a935a994ea36bf45007135341ad3781ccf9d0832acb458e799c31afa`; actual output SHA-256 is `ac5427adfcc362f4f758ae65f5fa53fe84f17ba3f01964663a98a7775e3200d4`.

**Domain limit:** this is a reference-lawful, canonical-derived counterexample, not a claimed default emission. The current one-control validator rejects it, and its 10 rows are below the advertised 12-row generator minimum. The canonical input itself already demonstrates the validator mismatch. To teach the full first-control rule, align the documented domain and validator with canonical distractor controls and include cases where spatial order and numeric order disagree.

### A3. Three legal exact overrides have no effect

At seed 17, sample index 0, difficulty `medium`, the default input is 16×19 with six color-6 cells. Each independently supplied legal override below returns a byte-identical grid:

| Override | Advertised global domain | Observed value |
|---|---|---:|
| `grid_h=22` | `12..22` | 16 |
| `grid_w=24` | `12..24` | 19 |
| `shape_size=7` | `3..7` | 6 |

All three returned grids pass `self_check`. Their common input SHA-256 is `b615b5bfdc1b2d26f57d43935739c6f3426f807efda453ea835e41a453cc216a`; the public Racket label is retained once for this identical input. The source selects dimensions and shape size directly from difficulty-dependent RNG ranges and never reads these three override fields. Honor these advertised overrides across their declared domains, or remove/redefine unsupported axes.

### Evidence and reproducibility

The bounded default search stopped at the first self-check rejection: seeds 0 through 131 inclusive, index 0, easy, 132 draws. This is a counterexample search, not a frequency estimate. Additional checks covered the three independent legal overrides, all five canonical pairs, and **four saved inputs labeled by public Racket**, all with valid outputs and no errors. No broad audit battery or hidden solve labels were used.

The complete inputs, actual outputs, rival outputs, exact differences, validator messages, anchor trace, canonical-fit counts, hashes, and command receipts are retained in [evidence.json](checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/evidence.json), with [input.json](checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/input.json), [racket.json](checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/racket.json), the source-bound [probe.py](checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/probe.py), and structured [commands.json](checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/commands.json). The Racket receipt is reference audit evidence, not training approval.

All recorded commands exited 0. Outer cwd was `/dev/shm/arc-round2-083747`; the wrapper's effective payload cwd was `/dev/shm/arc-round2-083747/WORK/repo`. The exact labeling invocation was:

```bash
TMPDIR=/dev/shm/arc-round2-tmp /workspace/scratch/6da8da487eb0/round2-venv/bin/python review.py run /workspace/scratch/6da8da487eb0/round2-venv/bin/python -m arcpuzzles apply 55ff88a3cf8f --input ../checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/input.json --out ../checks/audit/55ff88a3cf8f/racket.json --timeout 180
```

The source-bound `probe.py build` reconstructs the saved inputs and `probe.py analyze` verifies those inputs against the retained public receipt, checks canonical fit, and reproduces the stated comparisons. Use a new output path if rerunning public `apply`.
